title: Empowering Youth, Transforming India
body_text:
Amrit Peedhi for Viksit Bharat@2047
India is home to one of the world’s largest youth populations, with nearly 65 percent of its citizens below the age of 35. Over the years, the Government has expanded investment across education, skilling, employment, entrepreneurship, sports, health, and civic participation to convert this demographic advantage into a development dividend. Together, these efforts are enabling the Amrit Peedhi to shape Viksit Bharat @ 2047.
MY Bharat: A Platform for Youth-Led Development
At the centre of this vision is Mera Yuva Bharat, launched in October 2023 for youth aged 15–29. The technology-enabled platform brings volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, career support and civic participation into a single nationwide ecosystem.
Growing national platform – More than 2.22 crore youth have registered on the platform for volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling, and career opportunities, as of July 2026. Volunteering at scale – Over 1.52 lakh volunteering opportunities enable young people to participate in community service, environmental action, cultural initiatives and public programmes. Learning through experience – More than 24,900 experiential learning programmes have connected youth with governance, healthcare, media, technology and public service.
Digital Engagement and Civic Participation
Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 – More than 50 lakh youth participated through a nationwide quiz. The dialogue also involved 78 diaspora youth from 21 countries and identified 6,000 young leaders for a district-wise repository. National Service Scheme (NSS) – Volunteer enrolment increased from 34.09 lakh in 2014–15 to 38.90 lakh in 2025–26.
Education: Access, Quality and Future-Readiness
The education ecosystem has expanded while becoming more flexible, digital and innovation-driven. National Education Policy 2020 places the learner at the centre and links schooling, higher education, skills and employability.
One of the world’s largest school systems – India has 14.67 lakh schools serving 24.72 crore students, supported by more than 1.02 crore teachers. Improved retention – The secondary-school dropout rate declined from 14.54 % in 2013–14 to 7 in 2025–26. Digital classrooms – Over 1.49 lakh schools were covered under ICT and digital initiatives by 2025–26, with more than 1.76 lakh smart classrooms and 1.79 lakh ICT laboratories sanctioned (as of March 2026). Atal Tinkering Labs – More than 10,000 labs have engaged over 1.1 crore student innovators and supported more than 16 lakh projects.
Higher Education and Innovation
Rising enrolment – Higher-education enrolment increased from 3.4 crore in 2014–15 to 4.5 crore in 2023–24; Female enrolment increased 42.2% since 2014-2015 to 2.2 crores in 2023-24. Institutional growth
Incubation and research – 85 Atal Incubation Centres have created 32,000+ jobs and supported over 2,900 startups.
Flexible Learning and Digital Access
National Credit Framework – More than 700 universities and over 7,500 affiliated colleges have adopted the National Credit Framework (NCrF). Academic Bank of Credits – 3,123 institutions have been onboarded and more than 35.27 crore APAAR IDs issued, enabling learners to store, transfer, and redeem credits. (as on 12 th August 2026). SWAYAM – As on 12 th August 2026, the platform offers more than 20,370 courses and has recorded 6.5 crore+ enrolments. DIKSHA – Across India, 342 courses have recorded 19.06 crore enrolments, 15.02 crore completions, and the issuance of 13 crore certificates (as on 12 th August 2026).
Skilling and Employability
The Government has empowered over 6 crore people through its skilling initiatives. Skill India Mission has shifted training from basic certification towards a demand-led model connected with industry, apprenticeships, digital platforms, and emerging technologies.
Lower unemployment – The unemployment rate declined from 7.71 per cent in 2014 to 4.2 per cent in 2025. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) – More than 1.64 crore youth have been trained across four phases since 2015. PMKVY includes industry-linked training in AI, robotics, drones, electronics, green energy, and other future-facing sectors, with on-the-job exposure. Jan Shikshan Sansthan – 36.48 lakh people were trained till March 2026. National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) – More than 54.41 lakh apprentices were engaged till March 2026. Startup India – The number of startups grew from about 350 before 2014 to more than 2.47 lakh by August 2026, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme - As of 12 th August, 2026, the PM Internship Scheme has provided 1,64, 902 internship opportunities across 31 sectors. PM-SETU – Launched in October 2025 with an estimated outlay of ₹60,000 crore to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs through 200 hubs and 800 spokes, with industry participation and labor-market-led courses.
Between 2014 and 2025, ITIs increased from 9,977 to 14,688; enrolment from 9.5 lakh to 14.7 lakh; National Skill Training Institutes from 25 to 33; and Institutes for Training of Trainers from 11 to 120.
Sports and Fitness
India has built a structured sports pathway that begins with local talent identification and extends to high-performance support. Sport is increasingly seen as a viable career, backed by coaching, infrastructure, scientific training and competition exposure.
Khelo India infrastructure – Under the scheme, 349 infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore have been approved, alongside the establishment of 1,067 Khelo India Centres and 267 academies. The scheme also supports 2,745 athletes. Khelo India Games – Since 2018, more than 63,000 athletes have participated in the Youth, University, Winter, Para, Beach, Water Sports and Tribal Games. Support for elite athletes – The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports 51 Core, 52 Para Core and 130 Development athletes. Core and Development athletes receive monthly stipends of ₹50,000 and ₹25,000, respectively. Expanded investment – The revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced support for National Sports Federations have a combined outlay of ₹36,441 crore for the period 2026–27 to 2030–31.
Health and Well-being
Youth empowerment depends on physical, mental, and preventive healthcare. Government programmes have expanded adolescent-friendly services, mental-health counselling, substance-abuse awareness, and access to comprehensive primary care.
Adolescent health – Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics (AFHCs) increased from 6,619 in 2014–15 to 7,203 in 2021–22. Adolescents receiving clinical and counselling services rose from 39 lakh to 82 lakh in the same period; 97.67 lakh youth registered in the clinic in 2024–25 up to November 2024. Mental health – Tele-MANAS has handled over 43.70 lakh calls through 53 cells, supported by 23 mentoring institutes and five Regional Coordinating Centres (as on 12 th August 2026). Substance-abuse prevention – As on 12 th August, 2026, Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has reached over 30.05 crore people , including 11.86 crore youth. More than 28.56 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while over 28.29 lakh persons have received treatment and rehabilitation support.
A Decade of Transformation
Twelve years of sustained, multi-sectoral investment have produced a measurable transformation in India’s youth. More young Indians are staying in education, acquiring industry-relevant skills, entering formal employment, creating businesses, participating in community life, and competing at the highest levels of sport.
The shift has been from access to opportunity, from participation to leadership, and from youth as beneficiaries to youth as co-creators. Policy, institutions, and digital platforms have laid a strong foundation; the Amrit Peedhi is carrying it forward towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

enrichment.summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates a decade-plus of Indian government initiatives for youth empowerment across education, skilling, employment, sports, health and civic participation, framed under the 'Amrit Peedhi' (nectar generation) working toward 'Viksit Bharat@2047'. Key highlights include the Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform with 2.22 crore registered youth, NEP 2020-driven education reforms, skilling missions like PMKVY and PM-SETU, sports infrastructure under Khelo India and TOPS, and health initiatives like Tele-MANAS and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The release presents extensive statistics comparing 2014 baselines with 2025-26 achievements to demonstrate transformation in youth development outcomes.
enrichment.context:
India's demographic dividend—with nearly 65% of its population under 35—has been a central plank of government policy discourse, especially as the country aims to become a developed nation ('Viksit Bharat') by 2047, the centenary of independence. This backcrounder ties together multiple flagship schemes across ministries (Education, Skill Development, Youth Affairs and Sports, Health, Social Justice, Corporate Affairs) to present a unified narrative of youth-centric governance, a theme that resonates around occasions like Independence Day and International Youth Day.

Several schemes mentioned have standalone significance for exam preparation: the National Education Policy 2020 restructured India's education architecture including credit frameworks (NCrF, ABC/APAAR) and digital learning (SWAYAM, DIKSHA); Skill India Mission and PMKVY represent India's response to skill-gap challenges amid automation and Industry 4.0; Khelo India and TOPS reflect the sports governance ecosystem supporting Olympic-level athletes; and Tele-MANAS and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan address the growing policy focus on mental health and substance abuse, especially post-COVID. The Mera Yuva Bharat platform, launched in 2023, represents a newer digital governance model consolidating multiple youth engagement schemes (NYKS, NSS, etc.) into one ecosystem, reflecting the broader trend of digital public infrastructure (DPI) in Indian governance, similar to other 'India Stack' initiatives like UPI and DigiLocker.

prelims_questions.question: 'Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)' platform, mentioned in government youth empowerment initiatives, is intended for youth in which age group?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, Mera Yuva Bharat was launched in October 2023 for youth aged 15-29 years, bringing volunteering, skilling, leadership and civic participation into a single platform.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding government youth-related schemes: 1. PM-SETU aims to upgrade government ITIs through a hub-and-spoke model. 2. The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) provides monthly stipends only to Core athletes. 3. SWAYAM and DIKSHA are digital learning platforms under the Ministry of Education. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: PM-SETU (launched October 2025) upgrades ITIs via 200 hubs and 800 spokes; SWAYAM and DIKSHA are Ministry of Education digital platforms. Statement 2 is incorrect since both Core (₹50,000) and Development (₹25,000) athletes receive stipends under TOPS, not only Core athletes.

mains_questions.question: India's demographic dividend is often cited as a key advantage for its development trajectory. Critically examine the effectiveness of government skilling and education initiatives in converting this demographic advantage into productive human capital, with reference to schemes like Skill India Mission, PMKVY, and NEP 2020.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Social Justice / Human Resource Development

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of integrating digital platforms such as Mera Yuva Bharat, SWAYAM, and DIKSHA in India's governance framework for youth development. How do such platforms address challenges of access, scale, and accountability in public service delivery?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance: E-governance applications, models, successes, limitations
